action_summary: Four measured faults kept ordinary phrasings from reaching commands the machine can run. (1) The three wc rules required the counting word BEFORE the unit, so "Show the word count of the file X" bound nothing and capability selection answered it with docx.document.verify.intent_ooxml -- a Word-document verifier whose keywords include "word". (2) sha256sum answered only to "checksum", so "Compute the hash of the file X" reached source.evidence.extract.objective_grounded.stdlib and died with JSONDecodeError. (3) candidate_tokens scores registry keywords against the sentence's prose, so "Make a folder named X" scored no token at all -- route() returned OPEN__COMPOSER_NO_REACHABLE_TOKEN with tried=[] while extract_argv had already returned ['mkdir', X]; the same sentence saying "directory" worked, because that one word happened to be a keyword. (4) "Remove the duplicate lines from the file X" matched cp first and abandoned the whole table on the word "duplicate".

obs_solution.losing_routes_reason: REMOVING_THE_OFFENDING_KEYWORDS_FROM_THE_DOCX_VERIFIER was rejected: it would move this tie and leave the class, and the next capability with the word 'content' would reopen it. MAKING_THE_ADAPTER_TOLERATE_A_MISSING_SIDECAR was rejected: the verifier refusing is correct, and the defect is that it was chosen at all. REQUIRING_A_WRITE_CAPABILITY_TO_BE_NAMED_BY_THE_SENTENCE was rejected as a keyword rule of exactly the kind that measurably hijacks the scorer. APPLYING_THE_RULE_TO_ANY_SENTENCE_WITH_A_PAYLOAD_AND_NO_DESTINATION was rejected: that is the #6119 shape, where the only path in the sentence becomes the destination by default.

obs_verification.synthetic_verification_necessity: Every end-to-end row writes under canonical/astra_runtime/tmp with a directory name containing no English word and deletes the tree. The central test runs the SAME sentence twice, once with the destination absent and once with it already holding stale bytes, because that pair IS the defect -- a test that only ever wrote to a fresh path passed on baseline and proved nothing. The admission test asserts both directions, refusing the verifier and still admitting the writer, because a rule that fired on everything would be a deletion rather than a guard. The blast-radius test counts the trigger over seventeen ordinary sentences and pins the count at two.
